answer: Go to Reports in your site's dashboard and view the reports in the Stores section. To see items customers added to their cart but didn't purchase, use the Most Abandoned Products report (shows products placed in cart but not bought), the Abandoned Carts Funnel (shows how many carts were abandoned vs. recovered and total value), or the Abandoned Carts Summary (allows filtering by parameters like product gross value and can be downloaded). To see how items were sold, use Sales by Product Variant (shows which product variants like size/color sell the most), Sales by Product Category (breakdown of sales by category), Store Conversion Funnel (analyzes behavior from product view through added to cart to purchase), or Conversion by Product (shows how each product converts).

To rename a web link (menu item) in the Wix Editor: Click Pages and Menu on the left side of the Editor. Hover over the relevant menu item and click the More Actions icon. Then choose Rename to change the name of the item on your site menu.

To update the share image (og:image) and fix it if the change didn't appear: 1) Set the og:image in your Editor for the specific page (Pages & Menu > select the page > More Actions > Social share > Upload Image) or for the whole site (Website settings > General social image > Upload Image), then publish your site. 2) Use the platform-specific tool to refresh the cached preview: for LinkedIn, go to the LinkedIn Post Inspector (https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/) and enter your URL; for Facebook, use the Facebook Debugger and click 'Fetch new information' (or 'Scrape Again' if previously shared); for X use the X Card Validator; for Pinterest use the Pinterest Debugger. Note that LinkedIn may take up to a week to display the new image, and LinkedIn uses its own criteria to choose the best image for shares.

You can add a personalized name to your automated emails by using dynamic values (variables). In Wix Bookings, go to Booking Settings in your site's dashboard, click Emails & SMS notifications, hover over the relevant automation and click Edit, then click Edit under Create an email. To add the name in the email content, click the relevant text field, click + Add Dynamic Value on the Customize text panel, select the relevant value from the drop-down (such as the client's name), optionally enter fallback text (e.g., 'valued client') for when no data is available, and click Add. To add it to the subject line, click Edit next to the subject, click + Dynamic Value below the subject, select the value, enter fallback text, and click Add. Then click Save & Continue and Save. Note that personalized content does not appear in test email campaigns, but recipients will see it when the email is sent.

According to the documentation, Wix automatically creates a mobile-friendly version of your site using the content and elements from your desktop Editor; they are different views of the same site, not separate sites. If your site is not displaying correctly on mobile, first verify you are using a supported browser (Google Chrome or Safari) and operating system (iPhone: iOS 14 and above; Android: 9.0 and above), clear your browser's cache and cookies, and ensure you are viewing the site in portrait mode (Wix sites are only supported in portrait mode on mobile devices). Note that tablet devices such as iPads and Android tablets display the desktop version of your site, cropped within the vertical gridlines of the Editor; to resolve content being cut off, place your content within the vertical gridlines or use columns that are responsive to screen width. If you are experiencing specific alignment or structural issues on the mobile view, Wix automatically optimizes the mobile site to fit smaller screens, but you may need to adjust elements that do not align correctly across different rendering engines.

This behavior typically occurs when adjusting the scaling settings of a strip background image. In the Wix Editor, when you select a strip image and go to Settings > Scaling & Positioning, the 'How's the image scaled?' dropdown offers three options: 'Original Size' (where parts of the image may be cut off), 'Scale to Fill' (resized to fill space, may need repositioning), and 'Tile' (the image is displayed in tile formation across the available space, which appears as the image multiplying/repeating). To fix this, select the strip, click Change Strip Background (or Change Column Background), click Settings, scroll to Scaling & Positioning, and change the scaling option from 'Tile' or 'Original Size' to 'Scale to Fill', then adjust the position using the 'Where is it positioned?' grid to focus on the desired part of the image.

A 403 Forbidden error means you are unauthorized to view the page you are trying to access. To resolve it: 1) Make sure the URL (web address) you entered is correct. 2) Clear your browser's cache and cookies (you can also try opening the page in an Incognito/Private window first to test). 3) Go to the web address again. If the problem persists, contact Wix Customer Care and provide: the specific error with a screenshot, your Wix username/email, domain and site name, your operating system, browsers/versions tried, geographic location and ISP, internet security programs installed, and which troubleshooting steps you already tried.

Unwanted gaps at the bottom of your desktop page can occur between the page content and the footer, or below the footer on the live site. To remove a gap between page content and the footer, you can change the page design to a different preset, or adjust the page height by clicking and dragging the Adjust Page Height icon (if your page is covered in strips, click and pull the footer down first to access the main page area). If the gap appears below the footer on your live site, it may be because your page content is shorter than the current page length. You can resolve this by: changing the page background color to match the footer color, adding more content to the page to cover the viewport, resizing the footer to make it longer, or checking the Layers panel for hidden elements causing the gap.

If your dynamic list page shows items correctly in Preview but not alphabetically on the published live site, first ensure your site has been published since you added the sort conditions to the dataset. Additionally, verify that the dataset mode is set to 'Read' or 'Read & Write'; if the dataset is in 'Write' mode, it cannot read collection content or apply sort conditions. Note that dataset sorts override the order set by the 'Mirror on Site' feature, but they do not affect the order in your CMS collection views.

Users can check your calendar directly on your website by viewing the calendar app you have added to your site. If your subscription is in a grace period and recurring retries are enabled, the system automatically attempts to collect payment from your existing payment method (the same card) every 24 hours for the duration of the grace period. If you want to add text directly to the image (such as a tooltip that appears on hover), click the image, click the Settings icon, and enter your text in the 'Does this image have a tooltip?' field.

This is expected behavior: just as it takes search engines time to crawl and index new content, it also takes time for them to recognize that old URLs have changed or are no longer available, and the timing depends entirely on each search engine. Since you have already submitted removal requests and your updated sitemap, the remaining steps supported by the docs are: (1) make sure your site is verified with Google Search Console (via the Wix SEO Setup Checklist or manually), then in Google Search Console use Removals > New Request > Clear Cached URL for each old URL; (2) after sending each removal request, ask Google to crawl the page again by requesting indexing for that URL (you can also submit individual page URLs directly to search engines); and (3) wait, because Google must re-crawl the page before the saved version in its index is updated and the old result is removed. If you recently upgraded and connected your own domain, Wix automatically redirects the free Wix URL to your new domain, and search engines remove the free Wix URL once they detect the new domain during crawling.

If your documents are not being accepted, check the following requirements from the documentation: All documents must be issued within the same country you selected as your business location (documents from another country may be rejected). Your photo ID must be a color copy, and your name and date of birth must match exactly what appears on the ID. Address verification documents (such as utility bills) must have been issued within the last 6 months. You must enter a physical address (PO Boxes are not accepted). Double-check that your bank account number(s) are entered correctly. For business accounts, ensure your company name, registration number/tax ID, and Doing Business As name match your registered information and what appears on customer statements. To resubmit, go to Accept Payments in your dashboard, click Manage next to Wix Payments, click Edit Account Details, make corrections, click Save, then click Resubmit. Allow up to 7 business days for verification. If 7 business days have passed and you've confirmed all information is correct and matches your bank details, contact Wix Customer Care for further investigation.

Region or currency errors with Wix Payments typically occur when the currency set in your Wix account does not match the currency in your payment provider account, or when your business location is incorrect. To resolve this: 1) Ensure the currency in your Wix account matches your payment provider account currency. To change your Wix currency, go to Settings in your site's dashboard, click Language & Region, scroll down to Currency, select your currency from the drop-down menu, and click Save. 2) Check your business location at the top right of your dashboard; if incorrect, use the drop-down menu to change it. 3) Verify that your payment provider supports your region and currency—if your current provider does not support your desired currency, you may need to switch to an alternative payment provider that does.

To add a subscribe form to your site:

**In the Wix Editor:**
1. Go to your editor and click **Add Elements** on the left side.
2. Click **Contact & Forms**.
3. Scroll down to the **Subscribe** section and drag a form onto your site.
4. Click **Settings** to customize the layout, design, and manage submissions.

**In Wix ADI:**
1. Click **Add** on the top bar inside ADI.
2. Click **Section to Page**, then click **Subscribe** and select the layout you want to use.
   - To add the form to your footer (so it appears on all pages): Click the footer in the ADI builder and select the checkbox next to **Subscribe** on the left.

Once visitors fill out the form, they are automatically added to your contact list with a 'Subscriber' label.

To update the terms & conditions (policy agreement) checkbox at checkout in Wix Stores: Go to Checkout settings in your site's dashboard, then click Policies. Select the checkbox next to the policy you want to display and enter the policy text. To make customers agree to it before completing checkout, enable the 'Policy agreement checkbox' toggle. If you want the checkbox ticked automatically, also select the 'Checked by default' checkbox. Alternatively, from checkout settings click 'Customize your checkout', then Policies, select the policies you want to create, and enter the policy text. Note: as soon as you select the checkbox next to a policy and enter text, it is displayed in the footer of your Checkout Page.

If you followed the steps to change the Title tag in SEO basics but the browser tab title on your live site hasn't updated, first make sure you clicked Publish after entering the new title, as changes are not automatically reflected on the live site until published. Additionally, custom code added to your site may affect the browser tab title; try removing any custom code you added to see if the correct title appears. You can also check your live site in incognito/private browsing mode to rule out browser caching issues.

Since you have a Google Workspace Admin account, you can reset the password for your second business Gmail account as an admin. To do this: 1) Sign in to your Google Admin account. 2) Click Password, then Reset Password. 3) Choose to automatically generate the password or enter a password yourself. 4) (Optional) Click Preview to view the password. 5) (Optional) Enable the 'Ask for a password change at the next sign-in' toggle to require the user to change the password at next login. 6) Click Reset. 7) (Optional) Click 'Click to copy password' to paste it somewhere, such as in a Google Chat conversation with the user. 8) Choose to email the password to the user, or click Done. Note: By default, the password minimum length is 8 characters, which you can change in your organization's password requirements.

To connect Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to your Wix site: First, create a GA4 property in your Google Analytics account using the GA4 Setup Assistant (sign in, click Admin, select GA4 Setup Assistant, create the property, select your data stream, and copy your measurement ID under Web stream details). Then, in your Wix site's dashboard, go to Marketing Integrations, click View under Google Analytics, click the Show More icon in the top right corner, click Edit, paste your GA4 measurement ID in the pop-up (ensure no extra spaces), optionally select IP Anonymization, and click Save. Note that you need to upgrade your site and connect a domain before using Marketing Integrations.

For a page without a footer, click on the page itself and drag the 'Adjust Page Height' handle located at the bottom of the page to the desired position. Note that this option is only available if you have selected the 'No Header & Footer' layout for that page. If the handle isn't moving or the page won't resize, there may be an element at the bottom of the page preventing it from getting shorter (you cannot cut off elements). To fix this, use the Layers panel (bottom left of the editor) to locate and move or delete the blocking element first. You can also double-click the Adjust Page Height handle to reset the page height to its default.

It is not possible to edit or modify a domain name once it has been purchased. When you register a domain name, you reserve the letters or characters in that order. If you have already made the purchase, the only way to change the domain name (such as removing 'DBT') is to register a new domain. Important: Domains purchased through Wix are set to renew automatically, so you should turn off the auto-renewal option for the current domain to avoid paying for another year.

According to the documentation, it is not possible to restore deleted Wix Stores products. While you can view previously saved versions of your site and restore them in the Site History section, certain page types such as Wix Stores products cannot be restored this way. Additionally, Wix App collections (including Wix Stores) are not affected by CMS backups because they get their content from the relevant app.

To sync an external calendar (iCal) with Wix Hotels so visitors can book available dates, import your iCal URL into your Wix Hotels reservation calendar. The sync is one-way only (from the external iCal to Wix). Steps: 1) Go to your dashboard and click the Hotels tab. 2) Click to expand the Reservations tab and select iCal. 3) Click the Choose Type drop-down menu and select a room type. 4) Paste your iCal URL into the URL field. 5) (Optional) Click Add Calendar to add another room type and paste its iCal URL. 6) Click Save. Important: If you have multiple room types, you must add a different iCal URL for each room type. Note that this feature is not compatible with the Wix Hotels Channel Manager; if you want to use the Channel Manager, delete all URLs in this tab first.

To transfer the edited page from your copy site to the original site, use the copy and paste feature between Wix Editor sites: 1) Open the Editor of the copy site containing the edited page. 2) Click Menus & Pages on the left side of the Editor. 3) Right-click the relevant page and click Copy. 4) Open the Editor of the original site (target). 5) Right-click anywhere on the screen and select Paste (or select Paste & Apply Site Theme to apply the original site's color and text themes). 6) Rename the new page in the Pages panel if needed. Note: You can only copy regular pages—anchors, links, folders, lightboxes, router pages, and pages from third-party or Wix business solution apps cannot be copied.

To set one og:image for your entire site: open your site's settings, click Website settings, scroll down to General social image, click Upload Image, select an image (or click + Upload Media to upload a new one), click Choose File to add it, click Save at the top of the dashboard, then publish your site. The og:image is the image that appears when your page is shared on social networks (e.g., Facebook, X). The documentation does not specify whether this image is used when a link is posted in an email or on Instagram; it only covers social network sharing and link previews on platforms like Facebook, X, Twitter, Pinterest, LinkedIn, and WhatsApp.

To transfer an edited page from a copy version to your original site without overwriting the original page, copy the page in the copy site's Editor and paste it into the original site's Editor as a new page. Steps: In the copy site's Editor, click Menus & Pages on the left side, right-click the relevant page and click Copy. Open the Editor of your original site. Right-click anywhere on the screen and select Paste (or Paste & Apply Site Theme to apply the target site's colors and fonts). The pasted page is added as a new main page to the Site Menu; rename it by entering a new page name and clicking Done. The original page on the target site remains unchanged.

To download your website visit reports, go to All Reports in your site's dashboard, select the traffic report you want to view, click the Download drop-down at the top right, and select a file format (Excel, CSV, or Image/PNG). The documentation notes that Wix Analytics traffic reports allow you to analyze your site traffic over different time periods, though the specific steps to filter or download for a custom date range such as December 15 to January 15 are not detailed in the provided passages.

To cancel within the 14-day money-back period, go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account, click the More Actions icon next to the relevant plan, click Cancel Plan, and then click Cancel Now to confirm. If you cancel within the first 14 days, your plan ends immediately and you receive a full refund (allow up to 20 business days for it to appear on your statement).

Yes, Wix offers 800+ pre-set website templates (pre-designed designs) created by Wix designers. These templates include sample content, color themes, galleries, inner pages, and built-in business features. To use them: go to the Wix template gallery (organized by business categories), select a template that matches your style, and then customize every part in the Wix Editor using drag-and-drop. All templates are fully customizable—you can add, rearrange, or remove content and apps. You can also choose a blank template or wireframe template if you prefer to start from scratch. Templates are available for Wix Editor, Editor X, and Studio Editor, and all are responsive on different screen sizes.

To reassign your domain to a different site: Go to Domains in your Wix account and scroll to the relevant domain. Click the Domain Actions icon (or More Actions icon) on the right and select 'Assign to a Different Site'. Select the site you want to connect and click Next. If that site is currently connected to a different domain, choose whether to redirect your domain to the site's primary domain or replace the current primary domain, then click Assign.

To remove the default compressed references (-Xcompressedrefs) on a 64-bit JVM, set -Xnocompressedrefs as a generic JVM argument. This removes the lower 4GB memory restriction on Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks, allowing native memory to grow beyond 4GB. Note that this will significantly increase Java heap memory requirements (it is not uncommon to need 70% more heap space), so you should adjust the Java heap size (-Xmx) to a larger value and monitor/retune garbage collection. Use this only as a last resort after ruling out native memory leaks, as it allows native memory to grow unbounded.

Application code can override the HTTP session timeout by invoking the setMaxInactiveInterval() method on the HttpSession object; this setting overrides all other levels (Server, Enterprise Application, Web Application, and web.xml). To check for this, enable session tracing in WebSphere Application Server 7.0 using the trace specification: com.ibm.ws.session.*=all:com.ibm.ws.webcontainer.srt.*=all (add WAS.j2c=all:RRA=all for database persistence, or com.ibm.ws.drs.*=all for memory-to-memory persistence). The trace will show session management activity including any programmatic timeout changes.

IBM Security Bulletin swg21985013 covers CVE-2016-0394: IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker, upon installation on Unix platforms, set incorrect permissions for an object (the isadc directory), which could allow a local attacker to manipulate certain files. CVSS Base Score is 4.0 with vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N). Affected products are IBM Integration Bus V9 and WebSphere Message Broker V8. Remediation is APAR PI28139, available in IBM Integration Bus V9 fix pack 9.0.0.4 and WebSphere Message Broker V8 fix pack 8.0.0.6. As a workaround/mitigation for current V8 or V9 fix pack installations on Unix, run: find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \; ; find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \; ; find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type f -name *.sh -print -exec chmod 755
The Sybase Server Agent 620 FP2 installer (6.2.0-TIV-ITM_SYB-FP0002) can be downloaded from IBM Passport Advantage using part number CNN25ML.

The errors occur because the WebSphere Plug-in cannot locate the IBM Global Security Kit (GSKit) libraries required to initialize SSL/HTTPS transports. To resolve this, set the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable to point to the GSKit library directory that comes with the Plug-in. For a 64-bit Plug-in v8.x on Linux, use: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/IBM/WebSphere/Plugins/gsk8/gsk8_64/lib64/ . Note that on Linux, setting this from the command line prior to starting the web server may not work; instead, add the export command to /usr/sbin/envvars (for SLES/SUSE) or /etc/sysconfig/httpd (for RHEL) so the variable is set when the web server starts.

To resolve this error without installing a fix, perform the following local fix: 1) Open the WAS admin console. 2) Navigate to Resources > Resource environment providers > WP ScriptingService > Custom properties. 3) Locate the entry with the name "ServerExt.applications" and value "com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.ApplicationServerExtensions". 4) Delete this entry, save the changes, and restart the Portal server.

You can find the required authorizations by looking at the /IBMMON/AUTH profile available in the ITM transport imported into your SAP system. According to the technote, if you create your own userid instead of using the default IBMMON_AGENT, you must provide it with the same set of minimum authorization settings defined for the /IBMMON/AUTH profile. The specific authorization values may vary depending on the transport level, but the /IBMMON/AUTH profile in your transport contains the exact list needed for successful data collection.

Increase the value of the sib.trm.linger property in the sib.properties file to tune the messaging engine lookup delay so that the Work Load Manager (WLM) waits longer than the default three seconds before returning an error. Set the property in <WAS_HOME>/properties (applies to all profiles) or <PROFILE_ROOT>/properties (applies to all servers in that profile; this location takes precedence if defined in both). After changing the property, restart the server.
The transaction log gets corrupted when the IBM Content Collector server runs out of disk space.

In a clustered environment, after deploying an updated ruleapp with 'Replace RuleApp Version', the previous version may still execute if the hot deployment notification was not sent by the RES console or not received by all Execution Units (XU) in the cluster. Other possible causes include: the updated ruleset cannot be parsed successfully and RES falls back on an earlier active version that parses; asynchronous ruleset parsing is enabled, so while the updated ruleset is being parsed, an earlier version is used for executions; or the user publishing the update lacks sufficient administrative rights (Monitor role in WebSphere Application Server) to notify all Execution Units through JMX. Validate that the ruleset path requested does not specify a version (e.g., /MyRuleApp/MyRuleset/ requests the highest version) and check that all cluster nodes received the deployment notification.

The clearing event is being dropped because the EIF probe on the OMNIbus side is resetting/closing (<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after it receives the event, so the event never appears in the EIF logs and is not forwarded to OMNIbus. To resolve this, set the connection_mode in om_tec.config on the ITM Server (TEMS) to connection_less instead of connection oriented by changing 'ConnectionMode=co' to 'ConnectionMode=connection_less', then restart the EIF on your ITM using 'tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif'.

The error occurs because the Windows security policy 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing' is enabled, which is incompatible with the key import process (causing System.InvalidOperationException: This implementation is not part of the Windows Platform FIPS validated cryptographic algorithms). To resolve, navigate to Control Panel > Administrative Tools > Local Security Policy > Security Settings > Local Policy > Security Options, double-click 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing', disable the option, and then retry importing the keys. If the 'unable to validate parameters' issue persists on a new server, ensure encryption is fully set up by exporting the encryption keys and distributing the dc_ktf.xml file to the client folder for all clients. If the problem persists after disabling the FIPS option, contact IBM support for further assistance.

IBM Integration Bus Hypervisor Edition V9.0 and WebSphere Message Broker Hypervisor Edition V8.0 ship with Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Server 6.2, which is vulnerable to CVE-2017-14746, CVE-2017-15085, CVE-2017-15086, CVE-2017-15087, and CVE-2017-15275. Remediation: IBM strongly recommends contacting Red Hat to obtain and install fixes for Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Server 6.2, as applicable.

Yes. IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance can validate the signature of a Certificate Authority (CA) that signs a certificate using SHA-2 (SHA-256) while building the trust chain from the DataPower ValCred. This is supported on firmware versions 3.7.2, 3.7.3, 3.8, and 3.8.1.

The error IQQG0205E indicates that the version of the IBM FileNet Content Search Services (CSS) client embedded in the IBM FileNet Content Platform Engine (CPE) is not compatible with the CSS server version. For example, the log shows the client version (e.g., 5.2.0.2) is not in the list of client versions the server supports (e.g., [1.0.0.0, 1.5.0.0, 1.5.0.1, 2.0.0.0, 2.1.0.0]), and the server version is not in the list of server versions the client supports. To resolve this, the version of the CSS client files included in CPE must match the CSS server version. Check the readme files for your installed CPE and CSS fix packs, as they specify the required fix pack levels (for example, IBM Content Search Services 5.2.1.5 fix pack requires 5.2.1.5-P8CPE-FP005).

Look for the DATA #1 entry in the db2diag.log corruption message which contains the object identifier in the format Obj={pool:X;obj:Y;type:Z}. Here, pool is the Tablespace ID, obj is the Object ID, and type indicates the object type (0 = Table, 1 = Index). To find the object name, run the query: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=<ObjectID> and tbspaceid=<TablespaceID>". For example, for Obj={pool:3;obj:21;type:0}, run: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=21 and tbspaceid=3".

On a 64-bit JVM using compressed references, Native OutOfMemory (NOOM) can occur even when plenty of system memory is free because the problem is often a shortage of memory in the low-memory region (under 4GB), not overall system memory. The OS memory allocator freely allocates low-memory, so resources in the lower boundary can be exhausted. Even if the Java heap is located above 4GB, other data associated with Java objects (such as Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks) may be allocated in the low-memory region, and when the JVM tries to allocate memory for artifacts requiring 32-bit pointers in this depleted region, it throws an OutOfMemoryError. To resolve this, you can use -Xmcrs to increase the amount of low memory reserved at startup, or use -Xgc:preferredHeapBase=<address> to ensure the Java heap is allocated above the 4GB address space, leaving more room for Class Pointer and Monitor/Lock memory. Additionally, check ulimit settings for process/thread limits, as insufficient ulimit values can also cause NOOM with 'Failed to create a thread' messages.

WebSphere Application Server is loading the older JDBC driver class (ojdbc14.jar) due to a class collision. When multiple versions of the JDBC driver are configured in WebSphere Application Server, irrespective of the scopes, there is a possibility of a collision of the classes and the system cannot predict from which version of the driver jar the class got loaded. To resolve this, enable the "Isolate this resource provider" setting on each JDBC Provider configuration. When enabled, it ensures that only the jar specified in the classpath for that particular JDBC provider will be used for all datasources under it, preventing the older driver from being loaded.

The behavior is controlled by the transaction timeout, not the HTTP session timeout. For Rule Team Server (RTS)/Decision Center, the transaction timeout defaults to 10 minutes (600 seconds) and is configured via the context-param ilog.rules.teamserver.transaction.timeout in the teamserver web module's WEB-INF/web.xml (inside jrules-teamserver-<appserver>.ear\teamserver.war\WEB-INF). If a transactional operation takes longer than this value, the transaction is rolled back and the user is effectively kicked out of the operation. You should also check application-server-level transaction timeouts (for example, WebSphere Application Server's 'Maximum transaction timeout'), which can also cause rollbacks if exceeded.

This error occurs because the Centera SDK native library path is not loaded into java.library.path. Changes made to the setCenteraLibPath.sh (Linux/Unix) or setCenteraLibPath.bat (Windows) file were not picked up by the WebSphere startup script—often because the Content Engine was restarted from within the WAS console rather than from the command line, or the setCenteraLibPath script was not properly recognized when added to setupcmdLine.sh. To resolve, ensure the setCenteraLibPath script is correctly configured and included in the startup sequence, then restart WebSphere from the command line (or ensure a full restart that detects the changes) so the CenteraSDK path is loaded.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg22004378. The bulletin states that CVE-2017-1557 allows an authenticated user with authority to connect to a remote queue manager to send a specially crafted request that could cause a channel process to cease processing further requests, resulting in a loss of service for other connections serviced by the same channel process (CVSS Base Score: 4.3). Affected products include IBM MQ and IBM MQ Appliance v8.0.0.0 to v8.0.0.7, IBM MQ v9.0.0.0 LTS to v9.0.0.1 LTS, and IBM MQ and IBM MQ Appliance v9.0.1 CD to v9.0.3 CD. Remediation requires applying fix pack 8.0.0.8, fix pack 9.0.0.2, or IBM MQ 9.0.4 respectively. No workarounds or mitigations are available.

This is IBM Security Bulletin swg22003510 (CVE-2017-1236). Summary: IBM MQ could allow an authenticated user to potentially cause a denial of service by issuing/saving an incorrect saved channel status inquiry. CVSS Base Score 3.1; Vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L); temporal score at IBM X-Force vulnerability 124354. Affected products/versions: IBM MQ 9.0.2 CD, IBM MQ Appliance 9.0.x CD, IBM MQ 9.0 LTS; also IBM MQ and IBM MQ Appliance v8.0.0.0–v8.0.0.7, IBM MQ v9.0.0.0–v9.0.0.1 LTS, and IBM MQ/Appliance v9.0.1–v9.0.3 CD. Remediation: apply fix pack 8.0.0.8 (v8.0), fix pack 9.0.0.2 (v9.0 LTS), or IBM MQ 9.0.4 / CD update 9.0.4 or later (v9.0.1–9.0.3 CD and 9.0.2 CD). Workarounds/mitigations: for IBM MQ Appliance the affected queue manager must be restarted; for IBM MQ 8.0, 9.0 LTS, and 9.0.2 CD, restart the failed command server on the queue manager. No other workarounds are listed. Subscribe to My Notifications for future bulletins.

Sometimes encrypted and password protected documents cause document indexing errors. To identify them: 1. Login to Atlas database as PSSAPL user. 2. Run select * from ctx_user_index_errors;. 3. Copy the value in the ERR_TEXTKEY Field. 4. Run select * from documentlibrary where rowid='<value from Step 3>';. 5. This will list the document which has the indexing error.

This is a known DB2 11 for z/OS defect documented in APAR PI19804. The CIUSNTSR stored procedure contains a control statement with an IN-LIST predicate that references SQL variables. DB2 11 incorrectly processes SQL variables within IN-LIST predicates during CREATE PROCEDURE, causing SQLCODE -401 to be returned from DSNXOBFC (matching your SQLERRP value). Apply the available fix for APAR PI19804 (PTF UI20622) to correct the processing of SQL variables in IN-LIST predicates.

According to IBM documentation, IBM SPSS Statistics Subscription (newer releases) is not supported on Mac OS X 10.9.5 (Mavericks). The supported operating systems are: IBM SPSS Statistics 25 requires macOS High Sierra (10.13); IBM SPSS Statistics 24 requires OS X 10.10.x (Yosemite) through macOS 10.12.x (Sierra); and IBM SPSS Statistics 22 is supported on OS X 10.7 (Lion) and 10.8 (Mountain Lion), with OS X 10.9 (Mavericks) supported only after installing Statistics 22 FixPack 1. To resolve the 'installer not supported' error, you must either upgrade your Mac operating system to a supported version (10.10 or later for Statistics 24, 10.13 for Statistics 25) or use IBM SPSS Statistics 22 with FixPack 1 if you must remain on OS X 10.9.5.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg22012983: 'IBM MQ clients connecting to an MQ queue manager can cause a SIGSEGV in the amqrmppa channel process terminating it (CVE-2018-1371)'. The bulletin states that an IBM MQ client connecting to an MQ queue manager can cause a SIGSEGV in the queue manager's amqrmppa channel process, terminating it. CVE-2018-1371 has a CVSS Base Score of 6.5 with vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H). Affected products are IBM MQ V8.0 (maintenance level 8.0.0.8), IBM MQ V9 LTS (maintenance level 9.0.0.2), and IBM MQ V9 CD (version 9.0.4). Remediation: apply FixPack 8.0.0.9 for MQ V8.0, apply FixPack 9.0.0.3 for MQ V9 LTS, or upgrade to 9.0.5 for MQ V9 CD.

The error is caused by a corrupt installation of the CPE 5.2.1.2 .NET API. To resolve this, re-install the CPE 5.2.1.2 .NET API by: 1) Copying the software to a local disk, 2) Starting the re-installation of the .NET API, and 3) Selecting all sub-components of .NET framework 45 that were not listed before (select them all if unsure). During the next installation of ICC there will be no further errors regarding missing components.

The provided documentation does not contain specific information about making the 'where' filter in Workplace My Inbox case insensitive. While one Technote (swg21987296) notes that IBM Content Navigator metadata searches are case sensitive by default and that FileNet P8 repositories can use the 'Force Case Insensitive Search' flag on the object store, none of the retrieved passages address the specific behavior of the My Inbox where filter in Workplace or confirm whether that setting applies to it.

The resolver uses the digest to cache some URLs like resource aggregator collections, and the digest remains the same between restarts. Because of this, resources like theme files are served from the browser or proxy cache (HTTP 304) and not loaded from the server, which is why the old graphic persists until the user forces a refresh (Ctrl + F5). To force the updated theme resources to be loaded, set the "digest.seed" key in the WP ConfigService to any string value; this will be used in generating a new digest on server boot, causing different URLs to be generated so the updated resources are fetched from the server.

For IIB v10.0.0.9 and later, use the mqsichangeproperties command to generate a Java thread dump (javacore) against an execution group: mqsichangeproperties <Int.Node> -e <Int.Server> -o ComIbmInternalSupportManager/Java/JVM -n dump -v core. The -v core option produces a javacore (thread dump) on IBM JRE platforms (all platforms except HP and Solaris). Dump files are output to $MQSI_WORKPATH/common/errors. Note that collecting Java core dumps is invasive and will impact the performance of the Integration Server process.
